items.item: a ReplicaSet, not the Deployment object itself, is what actually creates and replaces pods; a Deployment manages a ReplicaSet which manages the pods
a StatefulSet's PVC-per-pod (volumeClaimTemplates) is what makes its storage follow a specific ordinal pod across rescheduling, not a shared volume
a headless Service (ClusterIP: None) gives DNS records for each individual pod rather than one virtual IP, which is what a StatefulSet actually uses for stable per-pod addressing

at.out: a Service-type detail beyond a refresher's one claim about name stability; named for a future topic's seam, not taught here

items.item: a ConfigMap has the same 'anyone who can create a Pod in the namespace can read it' exposure as a Secret — the difference is only that a Secret's base64 encoding and its name signal sensitivity, not that it is actually protected differently by default
a CSI (Container Storage Interface) driver is what actually implements dynamic provisioning for a given StorageClass; the StorageClass object itself just names which driver and parameters to use

multiple taints and tolerations on the same node require every taint to have a matching toleration before a pod may schedule there (unless a taint's effect is NoSchedule vs PreferNoSchedule, which differ in strictness)

items.item: a Job's pods default to restartPolicy OnFailure or Never (never Always), which is why a Job can actually reach a Completed state instead of restarting forever
etcd's Raft-based replication is what makes the API server's own writes durable across a control-plane node failure, which is why 'the declared state' survives a master restart
